name: Betahistine
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Betahistine is converted almost completely to the inactive metabolite 2-pyridylacetic acid (2-PAA), and about 85% of a dose is recovered in urine. The European label has no kidney trials but, based on post-marketing experience, states that no dose adjustment appears necessary in kidney impairment. Dialysis has not been studied. It has no US FDA label.
kidney_function_basis: SmPC does not grade kidney impairment; bands are shown on creatinine clearance (CrCl).

bands.recommendation: Usual dose: 8 to 16 mg three times daily with meals; maintenance usually 24 to 48 mg/day (SmPC).

hd: Not studied in dialysis (SmPC). Inactive metabolite likely accumulates; lowest effective dose if used.
monitoring: Clinical response; gastrointestinal upset (take with meals). Caution in asthma and peptic ulcer history (SmPC 4.4).

pediatric.approved_ages: Not for use under 18 years (insufficient data; SmPC).
